aspects.says: The check is best-effort: a removal made while an ArrayList walk is on its second-to-last element ends the loop silently and the last element is never visited.
basis: section:The Check Is Best-Effort: Some Changes Slip Past It

aspects.says: A walk over a ConcurrentHashMap that others change is not a view of one moment, so a total computed by walking can be one the map never held.
basis: section:A ConcurrentHashMap Walk Never Throws, and It Is Not a Snapshot

aspects.says: A ConcurrentHashMap iterator never throws ConcurrentModificationException and may or may not show keys added during the walk.
basis: section:A ConcurrentHashMap Walk Never Throws, and It Is Not a Snapshot
aspects.reason: which added keys a walk shows depends on hashing and resizing, so a test could only assert that it does not throw, which the quiz asks instead

aspects.says: A CopyOnWriteArrayList iterator's remove() throws UnsupportedOperationException; removal goes through the list.
basis: section:A CopyOnWriteArrayList Iterator Walks the Array It Started With

aspects.says: A CopyOnWriteArrayList iterator walks the array current when it was created: an element removed during the walk is still visited and one added is not.
basis: section:A CopyOnWriteArrayList Iterator Walks the Array It Started With

aspects.says: Iterator.remove() removes the element next() returned and resynchronises the iterator, so the walk carries on without skipping or throwing.
basis: section:Change a Collection During Its Own Walk Only Through the Iterator, or with removeIf

aspects.says: Across threads the fail-fast check promises nothing, so the exception is for finding bugs, never for program logic.
basis: section:The Check Is Best-Effort: Some Changes Slip Past It
aspects.reason: whether another thread's change is detected depends on timing and memory visibility, which no deterministic test can show

aspects.says: One thread changing a collection inside its own walk is enough to trip a fail-fast iterator; the exception is not about other threads.
basis: section:A Fail-Fast Iterator Checks a Counter on Every Step, and One Thread Is Enough to Trip It

aspects.says: During a walk, elements are removed through the iterator or with removeIf; the collection's own remove in a for-each throws or skips, and a forward index loop skips the element after each removal.
basis: section:Change a Collection During Its Own Walk Only Through the Iterator, or with removeIf

aspects.says: A fail-fast iterator copies the collection's structural-change counter when created and throws ConcurrentModificationException from the next step once the counter has moved.
basis: section:A Fail-Fast Iterator Checks a Counter on Every Step, and One Thread Is Enough to Trip It

aspects.says: Replacing a value (set, entry.setValue, put of an existing key) is not structural and does not trip a fail-fast iterator.
basis: section:A Fail-Fast Iterator Checks a Counter on Every Step, and One Thread Is Enough to Trip It
